sections.label: Scam cases and losses increase
sections.summary: Preliminary indicators show scam cases and losses would have risen about 10% and 40% in 2024 versus 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Preliminary indicators show that the number of scam cases and losses would have increased by about 10% and 40% respectively, in 2024, compared to 2023.

sections.label: Self-effected transfers share of scams
sections.summary: From January to September 2024, self-effected transfers accounted for 86% of scam reports and 94% of losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: From January to September 2024, self-effected transfers accounted for 86% of all scams reports and 94% of losses.

sections.label: Bill empowers Restriction Order powers
sections.summary: MHA tabled a Bill empowering Specified Officers to issue Restriction Orders to banks to restrict an individual's banking transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has, therefore, tabled this Bill to introduce new powers for the authorities to step in and stem further scam losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This Bill empowers Specified Officers, including Police Officers and Commercial Affairs Officers, to issue a Restriction Order (RO) to banks to restrict the banking transactions of an individual, if there is reason to believe that he will make money transfers to a scammer, withdraw any money and give it to a scammer or apply for a drawdown from any credit facility with the intention of benefiting a scammer.

sections.label: Notice of Amendment to Bill
sections.summary: MHA filed a Notice of Amendment to remove "substantially" from the scammer definition and "conducted remotely" from the long title.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: MHA has filed a Notice of Amendment, to remove the word "substantially" from the definition of a scammer in clause 2, as well as to remove the words of "conducted remotely" from the long title.

sections.label: Restriction Order directs banks
sections.summary: The RO will direct the bank not to execute banking transactions from an individual's account and not to allow credit drawdowns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The RO will direct the bank not to execute any banking transaction from an individual's bank account and not to allow any drawdown of credit facilities.

sections.label: Clause 5 limits RO duration
sections.summary: Clause 5 of the Bill limits the duration of a Restriction Order to a maximum of thirty days at the outset.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Second, clause 5 of the Bill limits the duration of an RO to a maximum of thirty days at the outset.

sections.label: RO extensions by Specified Officer
sections.summary: Clause 5 lets a Specified Officer extend the RO up to 30 days at a time, maximum five extensions, up to 180 days total.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 5 also empowers a Specified Officer to extend the RO for up to 30 days at a time, up to a maximum of five extensions, if the officer assesses that more time is required to persuade the individual.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The initial RO and five potential extensions will last up to a maximum of 180 days.

sections.label: Scam losses from willing transfers
sections.summary: From January to September 2024, willing transfers to scammers were 86 percent of scam reports and 94 percent of losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   From January to September 2024, cases where victims willingly transferred monies to scammers accounted for 86 percent of all scam reports and 94 percent of losses.

sections.label: RO validity and extension limits
sections.summary: The Bill states the RO is valid up to 30 days initially and can be extended up to five times, not exceeding 180 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: According to the Bill, the RO is valid up to 30 days at the outset and can be extended up to five times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The total duration will not exceed 180 days.

sections.label: Withdrawals for daily living and bills
sections.summary: The individual can apply to withdraw a fixed amount for daily living, medical bills and insurance premiums.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The individual can also apply to withdraw a fixed amount of money for the purposes of daily living, or to pay medical bills and insurance premiums.

sections.label: Speed and blocking suspicious transactions
sections.summary: The Bill lets officers issue ROs to block suspicious transactions, as speed is everything when it comes to scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, when it comes to scams, speed is everything.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill lets officers issue ROs to block suspicious transactions.

sections.label: Appeals decided on documents only
sections.summary: Clause 7(5)(b) allows appeals decided on documents alone without hearings, and clause 7(6) makes the Commissioner's decision final.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 7(5)(b) allows appeals to be decided based on documents alone – no hearings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Should they not get a chance to speak, especially for complex cases?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And under clause 7(6), the Commissioner's decision is final.

sections.label: Clause 6 fine
sections.summary: Clause 6 imposes a $3,000 fine for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 6 imposes a $3,000 fine for non-compliance.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses
sections.summary: In the first half of 2024, 26,587 scam cases were reported, with losses exceeding $385.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In just the first half of 2024, 26,587 scam cases were reported, with losses exceeding $385.6 million.

sections.label: Shared Responsibility Framework safeguards
sections.summary: Some safeguards are captured in the Shared Responsibility Framework, which took effect on 16 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some safeguards are captured in the Shared Responsibility Framework (SRF), which took effect on 16 December 2024.

sections.label: SRF bank investigation concerns
sections.summary: The speaker says addressing scams requires tailored strategies and frameworks, and is concerned about the SRF's reliance on banks to conduct initial scam investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Addressing such scams requires tailored strategies and frameworks, which I will come back to later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am concerned about the SRF's reliance on banks to conduct the initial investigation into scams, including assessing whether they have fulfilled their responsibilities.

sections.label: Independent investigative body proposal
sections.summary: An independent investigative body should be established to handle scam-related cases on banks' fulfilment of their SRF obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address these shortcomings, an independent investigative body should be established to handle scam-related cases pertaining to banks' fulfilment of their SRF obligations.

sections.label: Digital wallet fraud detection
sections.summary: Banks must be required to work with digital wallet providers to deploy real-time fraud detection algorithms monitoring all digital wallet transactions for anomalies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address this gap, banks must be required to work with digital wallet providers to deploy real-time fraud detection algorithms that monitor all digital wallet transactions for anomalies, including transactions that occur after the initial digital wallet set-up.

sections.label: Bank liability for losses
sections.summary: Banks should be held liable for losses if they fail to meet these duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Bank should be held liable for losses if they fail to meet these duties.

sections.label: Scam database and anti-scam ratings
sections.summary: The Police scam database should receive real-time updates from banks, telcos, social media and messaging providers, and MAS and IMDA should rate their anti-scam measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To address this, the scam database currently managed by the Police, should be allowed to receive real-time updates from the banks, telecommunications companies, social media platforms and messaging providers based on user reports, while incorporating robust safeguards to protect privacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MAS and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) should assess and rate financial institutions, telecommunications companies, social media companies and messaging platforms on the robustness of their anti-scam measures and their implementation of the systemic safeguards mentioned earlier.

sections.label: Rise in scam cases and losses
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2023 scam cases rose almost five times, with losses reaching $650 million in 2023 alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From 2019 to 2023, the number of scam cases increased almost five times, with losses reaching $650 million in 2023 alone.

sections.label: Restriction orders and police powers
sections.summary: The Bill grants powers to issue restriction orders to banks, restricting victims' transactions, and asks for stronger police powers and bank checking procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It offers certain protection and restricts victims of online and telecommunications fraud cases from conducting bank transactions to better protect them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Those who receive a restriction order will not be able to transfer money from their accounts, take out loans, and use ATMs or credit cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can the government consider giving the police stronger powers to reduce losses?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can the minister ask the bank to add a checking procedure to give the police and the bank more time to try to contact the person involved and make the necessary confirmation and explanations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The key idea embedded in the Bill is the granting of powers to issue ROs to banks to stop transactions as a last-ditch effort by the Police to prevent what has clearly adjudged to be a scam.

sections.label: How scams occur
sections.summary: Scams occur when an unwitting victim is manipulated to release information voluntarily or actively transfer or withdraw cash.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Scams, in contrast, occur when an unwitting victim is manipulated to either release such information voluntarily or, in the most egregious cases, abet the process altogether with active cash transfers or withdrawals.

sections.label: Distinction artificial and misleading
sections.summary: The distinction, while appealing in theory, is both artificial and misleading in practice.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The problem, however, is that this distinction, while appealing in theory, is both artificial and misleading in practice.

sections.label: Residents duped by scam offers
sections.summary: Meet-the-People Sessions encountered residents duped by discounted tour offers or job promises requiring paid pre-training.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In our Meet-the-People Sessions, we have encountered residents who were duped by offers of, say, a tour in Malaysia, offered at a discount, or the promise of a job, which involves specialised pre-training for a fee.

sections.label: Scam offences under Penal Code
sections.summary: The Schedule defines scams as offences under sections 416A, 417, 418, 419, 420, 420A and 420B of the Penal Code 1871, overlapping at section 420.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Scams are defined in the Schedule as offences falling under sections 416A, 417, 418, 419, 420, 420A and 420B of the Penal Code 1871.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The overlap is section 420 of the Penal Code.

sections.label: Thirty-day freeze period question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the 30-day freeze period activated by clause 5 of the Bill simply postpones the inevitable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What if the 30-day freeze period activated by clause 5 of the Bill simply postpones the inevitable?

sections.label: SRF relieves financial institutions burden
sections.summary: The passage states the SRF relieves financial institutions from solely bearing the burden of fraud if they fulfil a checklist of seemingly reasonable actions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps more concerning is how the SRF relieves financial institutions from solely bearing the burden of fraud so long as they fulfil a checklist of seemingly reasonable actions.

sections.label: SRF offers scant protection
sections.summary: The passage states the SRF as conceived offers accountholders scant protection from fraud even when customers make good-faith efforts to protect themselves.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: All this to say that SRF, as currently conceived, has offered accountholders scant protection from even instances of fraud, even when customers make good-faith efforts to protect themselves.

sections.label: Support for Bill and SRF refinement
sections.summary: The passage supports the Bill, notes reservations over ROs' intrusiveness, urges refining the SRF, and cites $385.6 million lost in the first six months of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would be similar in spirit to a grant of a letter of administration, albeit in a more limited sense.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would also essentially be an extension of the existing Money Lock feature, which already covers 61,000 accounts and $5.4 billion in savings, to designate a third-party as an authorised person with the ability to corroborate a genuine withdrawal intent.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The ROs put forward by this Bill are one way forward.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I have expressed some reservations over their intrusiveness and hope that there will be some exit option for those who, ex ante, insist on opting out.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I also urge this Government to not be content with the measures in this Bill alone, but to continue refining the SRF to build an ecosystem that is more resilient to scams and fraud.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That said, on balance, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the first six months of 2024, scam victims in Singapore lost a record high of over $385.6 million.

sections.label: Restricting scam victims' bank accounts
sections.summary: The Police could restrict a potential scam victim's bank account for 30 days, up to 180 days, with an opt-out provision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Eighty-six percent of scams in the first half of 2024 involved the voluntary transfer of monies by the victim to the scammer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: By allowing the Police to restrict a potential victim's bank account for 30 days in the first instance and up to 180 days in total, we will provide the Police, banks or family members with more time to convince potential scam victims that they may be at risk of being manipulated into sending money to scammers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That being said, the money in the bank accounts belong to the account holders and to uphold the principle that they have the right to determine its use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We suggest introducing a provision for individuals to opt out, subject to some safeguards.

sections.label: PSP proposes social worker input
sections.summary: PSP proposes the Bill require Police to consider social workers' opinions before issuing ROs, with victims counselled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP proposes that the Bill should stipulate that the Police must consider the opinions of social workers before issuing ROs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Scam victim should receive counselling from social workers who can, with the assistance of the victim's family members, determine whether the RO would cause harm to the victim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will better help the Police decide whether the RO is beneficial for the victim.

sections.label: Bill empowers Police to issue ROs
sections.summary: The Bill lets Police issue ROs to banks restricting scam victims' transactions when transfers to scammers are reasonably believed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The onus is also on Singaporeans to remain vigilant and take steps to protect themselves from potential scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We hope that after this Bill is enacted, we will be able to prevent more victims from voluntarily transferring funds to scammers, which will hopefully reduce the attractiveness of Singapore as a target for scammers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed Bill seeks to protect targets of ongoing scams by empowering the Police to issue ROs to banks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These ROs have the effect of restricting the banking transactions of scam victims and they will be issued if there is a reasonable belief that the victims concerned will make money transfers to scammers or utilise credit facilities to benefit them.

sections.label: RO before actual financial loss
sections.summary: Read with clause 4, an RO could theoretically be issued before the intended victim suffers any actual financial loss.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Read together with clause 4, this, theoretically, has the effect of enabling the issuance of an RO, even before the intended victim has suffered any actual financial loss.

sections.label: Definition of relative excludes parents
sections.summary: A question asks why parents are left out of the definition of a relative in relation to a scam victim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My fourth question has to do with the definition of a relative in relation to a scam victim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that parents are left out of the definition and could I ask the Minister why this is the case?

sections.label: Eyeyah scam prevention magazine
sections.summary: Eyeyah partnered Meta, SPF, the National Crime Prevention Council and CSA on a 44-page scam prevention magazine for students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In December last year, Singapore art, animation and design educational platform Eyeyah partnered Meta, SPF, the National Crime Prevention Council and the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore to come up with a 44-page, a very artistically designed magazine for students which was focused on scam prevention.

sections.label: Scam identification magazine for students
sections.summary: 40,000 free hard copies of a magazine on identifying scams will be distributed to students via school art clubs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These are critical skills in identifying potential scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that 40,000 hard copies of the magazine will be distributed for free to students through primary and secondary school art clubs.

sections.label: Arts, loneliness and Jun Yang Pow
sections.summary: A UK report found older arts participants benefited from meeting people, and Jun Yang Pow held a Suntec City exhibition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a 2012 report by the Baring Foundation in the UK, entitled "Tackling Loneliness in Older Age – The Role of the Arts", older participants frequently noted that their first significant benefit from arts projects was meeting new people, forming friendships and feeling less isolated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have another example I would like to talk about from this past weekend.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This past weekend, terminally ill artist Jun Yang Pow held an exhibition entitled "Canvas of Memories" at Suntec City celebrating his artistic and personal journey.

sections.label: Scam victim losses in Jalan Kayu
sections.summary: Victims lost over $385.6 million in the first half of last year, including residents in Jalan Kayu.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Over the first half of last year, victims lost more than $385.6 million, which is a substantive sum of losses that impact victims very significantly, some of whom are my residents in Jalan Kayu.

sections.label: Clause 3 limits on ROs
sections.summary: Clause 3 limits ROs to directing banks to prohibit transfers or withdrawals and to prohibit credit facility drawdowns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under clause 3 of the Bill, RO is limited to the extent of directing banks in: one, to prohibit a transfer or withdrawal of money from any bank account of a scam victim maintained with that bank; or two, to prohibit the granting or allowing a drawdown of any credit facility to the scam victim.

sections.label: Expanding ROs to platforms
sections.summary: The member asks whether MHA will consider expanding ROs to cryptocurrency exchanges, remittance companies, e-commerce and e-wallet providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to ask if MHA will consider expanding the scope of ROs to include platforms, such as cryptocurrency exchanges, remittance companies or e-commerce and e-wallet providers?

sections.label: RO risks, daily funds, Money Lock
sections.summary: The member asks about RO unintended consequences, daily expense access, and notes Kill Switch and Money Lock safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On this aspect, I am keen to understand the unintended consequences that may be caused by the issuing of RO, on how we can mitigate the potential risks of the ROs while minimising inconvenience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope to clarify if there would be mechanisms to allow individuals issued with ROs to access limited funds for daily expenses, for example, up to a reasonable cap while investigation is underway.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Currently, the Government has worked with banks to provide mechanisms, such as the Kill Switch and Money Lock, as safeguards to protect the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These measures provide banks' customers with proactive options to secure accounts through either freezing their bank accounts if they suspect their accounts are compromised or set aside a sum of monies that cannot be transferred out of their bank account via online means.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is a positive sign when more than 181,000 customers have used the Money Lock to protect their money to set aside close to $15.8 billion in savings, out of reach of potential scammers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can further encourage adoption across different demographics, especially among the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These mechanisms can complement the issuance of ROs to address cases where scams progress despite these safeguards.

sections.label: Scam losses and willing transfers
sections.summary: In the first six months of 2024, $385 million was lost to scams, a 25% increase, with 86% involving victims willingly transferring money despite warnings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The urgency of this problem is underscored by the fact that just in the first six months of 2024, a staggering $385 million was lost to scams, which is a 25% increase from the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Disturbingly, 86% of these scams involved victims willingly transferring money despite repeated warnings from banks, law enforcement and loved ones.

sections.label: Protection from Scams Bill purpose
sections.summary: The Protection from Scams Bill empowers the Police to issue temporary ROs as a last resort to protect potential victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Protection from Scams Bill addresses this urgent and escalating challenge by empowering the Police to issue temporary ROs as a last resort to protect potential victims.

sections.label: Police temporary RO powers
sections.summary: The Bill enables the Police to issue temporary ROs to prevent further victimisation of individuals at risk of falling prey to scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill aims to empower law enforcement, specifically, the Police, to intervene more effectively by enabling them to issue temporary ROs to prevent further victimisation of individuals at risk of falling prey to scammers.

sections.label: Police ROs to banks
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Police to issue ROs to banks to restrict an individual's banking transaction if there is reasonable belief of transfers to scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a crucial step towards protecting our citizens and businesses and ensuring a safer, more secure society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill empowers the Police to issue ROs to banks to restrict an individual's banking transaction if there is reasonable belief that the individual will make money transfers to scammers.

sections.label: Scam claimants age data
sections.summary: The figures reflect life savings and well-being of Singaporeans, and data shows 72% of scam claimants are between 31 and 60 years old.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These figures are concerning, as they reflect not just credit and debit balances on a bank statement, but the life savings and associated financial, social and emotional health and well-being of thousands of fellow Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, data shows that 72% of the scam claimants are between 31 and 60 years of age.

sections.label: Voluntary transfers in scams
sections.summary: In the first six months of 2024, 86% of scams involved victims voluntarily transferring funds based on false but sincere trust.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the first six months of 2024, 86% of scams involved victims voluntarily transferring funds based on false but sincere trust, including love scams, investment fraud and impersonation schemes.

sections.label: Stopping people using own money
sections.summary: The speaker says they know better than legally competent people and will stop them using their own money, and seeks clarification on who must convince the individual and what exhausting attempts means.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are, in fact, saying that we know better than them and that despite their legal competency, we are going to stop them doing what they want to do with their own money.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support this approach, yet, seek clarification about who is responsible for attempting to convince the individual and what is meant by those attempts being exhausted.

sections.label: Scam losses in Singapore
sections.summary: In 2023 Singapore lost $650 million to scams, and in the first half of 2024, 86% of reported scams were self-effected transfers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2023 alone, in Singapore, an astonishing $650 million is lost to scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Alarmingly, in just the first half of 2024, 86% of reported scams were the result of self-effected transfers.

sections.label: Average losses in scam types
sections.summary: GOIS victims lost on average more than $100,000 per case, while investment scams saw average losses of over $40,000 per case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On average, victims of GOIS lost more than $100,000 per case while investment scams saw average losses of over $40,000 per case.

sections.label: Fine for contravening restriction order
sections.summary: Clause 6 of the Bill makes banks that contravene a Restriction Order liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Furthermore, clause 6 of the Bill stipulates that banks which contravene an RO shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $3,000.

sections.label: Scam losses and self-made transfers
sections.summary: In 2023 Singapore lost $650 million to scams, and in the first half of 2024, 86% of cases involved transfers made by the victims themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2023, Singapore lost $650 million to scams, and in the first half of 2024, 86% of cases involved transfers made by the victims themselves.

sections.label: Resident scam cases and Bill support
sections.summary: A Pasir Ris-Punggol resident lost $3,000 and another lost over $50,000 to a love scam, and the speaker supports the Bill empowering Police to issue Restriction Orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, a Pasir Ris-Punggol resident lost $3,000 despite reporting the fraudulent transaction to the bank, which still allowed the transfer to be made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Another fell victim to a love scam, losing over $50,000 despite her family's attempts to stop her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These cases demonstrate the manipulative nature of scams that exploits victims' emotions and trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I support the Bill that empowers the Police to issue Restriction Orders (ROs) to stop such transactions.

sections.label: Restrictions on bank accounts
sections.summary: MHA will first impose restrictions only on bank accounts and credit facilities, addressing many scam cases and reducing fund flows to scammers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MHA recognises that there is a risk that such entities can also serve as intermediaries in the scam chain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: However, as a start, we will impose restrictions only on bank accounts and credit facilities, which would address a significant number of scam cases and reduce the risk of fund flows to scammers.

sections.label: RO as last resort
sections.summary: The RO is a last-resort, temporary measure, issued for a maximum of 30 days and extended up to five times, then lapsing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As pointed out by Ms Ng and Ms Poa, it is indeed our policy intent to balance between protecting an individual from harm and respecting the individual's autonomy and personal responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And this is why the RO is meant to be a measure of last resort and is only issued temporarily – for a maximum of 30 days at the outset and extended up to five times if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The RO will lapse after the maximum number of renewals, even if the individual remains set on transferring monies to the scammer.

sections.label: RO scope of restriction
sections.summary: The RO restricts only the individual's banking transactions and credit facilities, not those of a third party assisting transfers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The RO will only restrict banking transactions and credit facilities of the individual, but not that of a third party assisting an individual to make monetary transfers.

sections.label: ROs on joint accounts
sections.summary: Because banks said implementing a proposal was operationally challenging, ROs will be imposed on both types of joint accounts for a start.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Ms Hazel Poa asked if ROs would be applicable to joint accounts and noted that doing so would inconvenience the joint account holders who are not subject to an RO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: There are two types of joint accounts: Joint-Alternate accounts where each account holder can perform banking transactions without the consent of the other account holders and Joint-All accounts where all account holders must give their instruction for any bank transaction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: However, the banks have informed us that it would be operationally challenging for them to implement such a proposal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Hence, we have decided to impose the ROs on both types of joint accounts for a start.

sections.label: Family, social workers, police report
sections.summary: Family members may bring social workers and counsellors, but an RO is not contingent on a police report by third parties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Family members may also bring in social workers and counsellors to help convince the victim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: That said, the issuance of an RO is not contingent on a police report by a family member or other third parties, as this may not be necessary and may even delay our efforts to protect our victim.

sections.label: Expected RO issuance numbers
sections.summary: Based on Police experience, five to 10 ROs per month are expected, mainly for scam victims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, based on the Police’s experience, we expect to issue five to 10 ROs per month, mainly for scam victims.

sections.label: Access to money for living expenses
sections.summary: An individual subject to an RO may apply to Police for a fixed amount of monies for living expenses, processed within hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: However, we are also mindful that the scammer may exploit any channel through which the individual can gain access to money.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will therefore take a risk-calibrated approach, by allowing an individual who is the subject of an RO to apply to the Police for access to a fixed amount of monies for living expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Our intent is to ensure that this is done as quickly as possible – we are talking about hours, not days.

sections.label: Applying to vary an RO
sections.summary: An individual needing more money can apply to Police to vary the RO for a specific transfer or withdrawal with proof of need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If the individual requires additional amounts of money, the individual can apply to the Police to vary the RO to allow a specific transfer or withdrawal by showing proof of the need to access these amounts.

sections.label: Police internal controls for ROs
sections.summary: The Police will institute internal controls placing initial approving authority for ROs with the Director or Deputy Director of the Commercial Affairs Department.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Police will institute internal controls such that the initial approving authority for ROs will reside with the Director of the Commercial Affairs Department or, in his absence, a Deputy Director of the Commercial Affairs Department.

sections.label: Bank immunity for complying with ROs
sections.summary: A bank and its officers are protected from criminal and civil liability for complying with an RO with reasonable care and good faith.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: A bank and its officer, employee or agent will be protected from criminal and civil liability for any act or omission in complying with an RO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The immunity applies only if the act was done or the omission was made with reasonable care and in good faith.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if imposing a fine of up to $3,000 on banks for contravening an RO without reasonable excuse is sufficient.

sections.label: Withdrawal for basic sustenance
sections.summary: Upon application to the Police, an individual will be allowed to withdraw a fixed sum reasonable and sufficient for basic sustenance, including bill payments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Upon application by an individual to the Police, he will be allowed to withdraw a fixed sum of money, which will be reasonable and sufficient for basic sustenance, including their bill payments, which I had mentioned earlier.

sections.label: Banks co-located with ASCom
sections.summary: Since 2022, ASCom and MAS have worked with major retail banks to co-locate bank staff with ASCom, enhancing real-time coordination with Police.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Since 2022, the ASCom and MAS have worked with the major retail banks in Singapore to co-locate the banks' staff with ASCom.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This has greatly enhanced the banks' real-time coordination with the Police to distinguish a scam from a legitimate transaction, trace fund flows and freeze bank accounts suspected to be involved in scammers' operations.

sections.label: Police ties and public education
sections.summary: Police work with INTERPOL and counterparts, and the ScamShield Suite was launched for public education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Police have strong operational ties with their counterparts in key jurisdictions and work with international organisations, such as the INTERPOL, to exchange information and conduct joint investigations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But, importantly, it would be even better to prevent such scams from materialising in the first place and this is why we fully agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng that public education is a critical area of work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We recently launched the ScamShield Suite to make scam resources easily accessible to the public.

sections.label: Restriction orders versus scam cases
sections.summary: The Minister of State said Police expect five to 10 ROs a month, negligible against about 50,000 annual scam cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: The Minister of State mentioned that the Police expect to issue five to 10 ROs a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: So, that is about 60 to 120 a year, but this is negligible compared to the approximately 50,000 scam cases reported annually.

sections.label: Losses per scam case
sections.summary: Government official impersonation, investment and love scams showed average losses per case of $150,000 to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: When we looked at the cases, in particular, when we looked at government official impersonation scams, we looked at investment scams, we looked at love scams, we are looking at losses per case of between, on average, $150,000 and $1 million.

sections.label: Possible expansion of restriction orders
sections.summary: The RO could cover cryptocurrency exchanges, remittance companies and e-wallet providers, but restrictions now apply only to bank accounts and credit facilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the second point that the Member raised, I mentioned in my speech that the RO could be expanded to include other entities, such as cryptocurrency exchanges, remittance companies and e-wallet providers, should scammers shift their tactics to exploit these platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, we recognise that there is a risk that such entities can also serve as intermediaries in a scam chain, but for a start, we are imposing restrictions only on bank accounts and credit facilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But we will continue to work with MAS to monitor the scam situations and we will consider expanding the scope of the RO in future if necessary.
